lead: Teleoperation is the fastest way for a humanoid to do a new task and to collect demonstrations for a VLA. The operator moves their arms in a VR headset and the robot repeats them; delay is what ruins it. In this lesson you teleoperate both of the G1's arms with a script and measure the latency at which everything falls apart.
objetivo: teleoperate both of the G1's arms through a script of targets with latency and measure how many targets the hand reaches.

aprende.t: The path of a gesture: VR, network, whole-body control, joint
Latency × reference horizon: don't confuse it with SONIC's 80 ms
Arm reach: the target that no latency can save
Teleop as data collection for VLA (TWIST2, GR00T-WBC)

hero_alt: Operator seen from behind, wearing a virtual reality headset with two controllers raised; in front, a humanoid robot with a dark visor repeats the gesture.

itens.t: pose of the hands and head

nos.detalhe: The VR headset measures the pose of the operator's head and hands. TWIST2 used a PICO 4U and a roughly US$ 250 2-DoF neck on the robot, and reported 100 demonstrations in 15 min (reported, arXiv Nov/2025).
Everything that happens between the gesture and the robot receiving the target: sensor reading, network, preprocessing and inference. In the kit, a single number (--latencia-ms).

Every 20 ms the controller redoes the IK of both arms from the measured state, with the legs in the standing pose. In SONIC, the same role is played by a policy that receives the operator's pose as the reference.
The G1's PD brings each joint to the requested angle. The target counts as reached when the hand gets within 3 cm of it inside the 0.6 s window.

secoes.legenda: Teleop is a closed loop with a human in it: a big delay makes the operator correct what has already passed.

secoes.titulo: Three things the 2026 research makes clear

texto: SONIC has a "low latency" checkpoint (06/16/2026) that looks 4 future frames ahead at 20 ms: about 80 ms of reference horizon. The default checkpoint looks 10 frames ahead (about 200 ms).
The README itself warns: these numbers are not the total teleoperation latency, which includes sensor, network, preprocessing and inference.
The GR00T-WholeBodyControl repository ships VR teleop with PICO, CloudXR inside the process via isaacteleop[cloudxr] (06/16/2026) and IsaacTeleop 1.4 with Jetson AGX Orin (09/14/2026).
On 05/07/2026 it gained the end-to-end VLA flow on the G1: collect with teleop, fine-tune GR00T N1.7 and deploy with SONIC.
HOVER (ICRA 2025, reported) distilled several command modes (VR, mocap, exoskeleton, joystick) into one policy of about 1.5M parameters.
SONIC uses a single token space for VR, human video and VLA: the same controller obeys any of them (lesson 7).

secoes.titulo: Teleoperate both arms from a script
secoes.sub: The kit/passos.json script plays the operator's role: six controller offsets, alternating hands. The sixth, on purpose, asks for 60 cm forward.

blocos.conteudo:
F=${FTH:-$HOME/fth}; cd $F/corpo-inteiro && . $F/.venv/bin/activate
python3 kit/teleop_sim.py --roteiro kit/passos.json; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
latência do operador ao robô: 80 ms · tolerância: 3 cm · controle a 50 Hz
alvo 1 · t=0.2 s · mão direita  · atingido em 162 ms
alvo 2 · t=0.9 s · mão esquerda · atingido em 160 ms
alvo 3 · t=1.6 s · mão direita  · atingido em 174 ms
alvo 4 · t=2.3 s · mão esquerda · atingido em 154 ms
alvo 5 · t=3.0 s · mão direita  · atingido em 166 ms
alvo 6 · t=3.7 s · mão direita  · não atingido (chegou a 21.7 cm)
robô de pé: sim
alvos atingidos: 5/6
saída: 0

Each target takes about 80 ms of latency + 80 ms of motion. The 6th is not reached at any latency: it is out of the arm's reach.

ERRO no roteiro: mão 'esquerdo' (use direita ou esquerda)
saída: 1

The script accepts only "direita" and "esquerda". A typo stops before touching the robot, not in the middle of a session.

alvos atingidos: 6/6

The 6th target with dx 0.25 instead of 0.60: all reached.

secoes.sub: The same script with five latencies. Each target's window is 0.6 s.

blocos.conteudo:
F=${FTH:-$HOME/fth}; cd $F/corpo-inteiro && . $F/.venv/bin/activate
for ms in 0 80 300 450 550; do
  echo "$ms ms → $(python3 kit/teleop_sim.py --roteiro kit/passos.json --latencia-ms $ms | tail -1)"
done

abas.html:
0 ms → alvos atingidos: 5/6
80 ms → alvos atingidos: 5/6
300 ms → alvos atingidos: 5/6
450 ms → alvos atingidos: 4/6
550 ms → alvos atingidos: 0/6

Up to 300 ms there is window to spare. At 450 ms one target already misses the window; at 550 ms none is reached in time. With a real operator, the effect shows up sooner: they start correcting for the delay.

exercicios.texto: Run teleop with the kit's script and 80 ms.
Copy the script to ~/fth/movimentos/passos-meu.json and bring the 6th target within reach (dx less than 0.3).

exercicios.titulo: E3 · The latency that zeroes everything
exercicios.texto: Run the latency sweep and say, in one sentence, why 550 ms zeroes everything with a 0.6 s window.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: SONIC's low-latency checkpoint has 4 frames at 20 ms. What are those 80 ms?
opcoes: The total latency, from the operator's gesture to the robot's movement.
The time the VR headset takes to measure the hand.
The future reference horizon the controller observes.
The PD loop period of the G1 joints in this mode.
perguntas.explica: This is how much of the future reference the policy sees. The README says it is not the end-to-end latency, which adds up sensor, network, preprocessing, and inference.

perguntas.p: Target 6 is not reached even with zero latency. What does that tell you?
opcoes: That control at 50 Hz is too slow for this target.
That the target is out of the arm's reach; latency does not change that.
That the script has the wrong hand name for this target.
That the robot fell before target 6 and stopped responding.
perguntas.explica: 60 cm in front of the hand is beyond the G1's arm length. The hand gets to 21.7 cm and stops: the IK does the best it can within the limits.

perguntas.p: What is whole-body teleoperation good for besides operating the robot in real time?
opcoes: For collecting demonstrations and fine-tuning a VLA (GR00T N1.7 + SONIC).
For measuring the robot's battery during a usage session.
For calibrating the depth camera in the robot's head.
For nothing beyond that: teleop data is not reused for training later.
perguntas.explica: Teleop is the source of task data: TWIST2 reported 100 demonstrations in 15 min, and GR00T-WBC has the flow collect → fine-tune N1.7 → deploy with SONIC.

itens.texto: Gesture, network, whole-body control, joint: each step adds delay.
Reference horizon is not end-to-end latency.
Teleop is how you collect the demonstrations that train the VLA.
